newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr at 34-month high on mark, bourses bullish.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr at 34-month high on mark, bourses bullish.

text.p: The dollar rallied to a 34-month high against the mark on Tuesday as a combination of German unemployment gloom and U.S. economic optimism continued to attract funds to U.S. securities.

There was renewed bullishness on European equity markets, too, after Wall Street closed up following three consecutive tumbles. London, Frankfurt and Paris stocks all opened sharply higher and Frankfurt soon put on some 1.5 percent to score a new trading peak.

Currency market analysts said there was little fresh news overnight to account for the latest dollar push higher, but the yawning gap between 10-year U.S. and German bond yields, now 1.15 percentage points in favour of the dollar, was a major driving force.
"We feel dollar/mark has miles to go yet," said Peter Von Maydell, currency economist at UBS. The last time the bund/T-note spread was this wide was 1989 when dollar/mark was at 1.88.
At 1015 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.7115 marks, up well over a pfennig from the close in Europe on Monday at 1.6941 marks. Against the yen, it was at 122.12 compared with 120.92 late Monday.
The dollar rally also subdued the mark in Europe against the lira and peseta.

Von Maydell at UBS said the dollar had been well bid since the first of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimonies to Congress last Wednesday. Greenspan said a pre-emptive interest rate rise could not be ruled out and this sent U.S. long-term yields sharply higher.
German yields have not followed suit because labour market concerns there mean the Bundesbank is not likely to raise interest rates any time soon.
A bigger-than-expected rise in the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management's February business activity index on Monday underlined the relatively brisk pace of U.S. growth, analysts said.
The second leg of Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins will be delivered on Wednesday, while the Fed chairman was due to testify to the house budget committee at 1500 GMT on Tuesday.
On Wall Street overnight the Dow Jones industrial average jumped 41.18 points to 6,918.92 after losing more than 160 points over the previous three sessions.

European bourses responded with relief: London shares started higher, although buying was still tentative, and the blue chip FTSE 100 index soon put on more than half-a-percent, moving within 30 points of its all-time high of 4,362.4, set on 20 February.
But, analysts said market nerves ahead of Greenspan's testimony on Wednesday and U.S. jobs numbers on Friday should put a cap on near-term gains.
"Wall Street once again has come to the rescue but there are still a few minefields to cross before the week is out," the head of trading at a major investment bank said.

In Frankfurt Germany's DAX index pushed into new record territory above 3,300 points, boosted by the strength of the dollar -- which makes exports more attractive. A rally in the car sector following bullish noises from Daimler on its 1996 and 1997 results.
However, as with London, dealers were still wary ahead of Greenspan's next pronouncements.
On the Paris bourse the bulls were also rampant. French shares opened with a near one percent jump and then moved higher on the back of the firm dollar and resurgent Wall Street.

"Everything is looking fine. Confidence is coming back while we are awaiting the U.S. statistics at the end of the week. As long as the dollar holds up, there is no reason why the market should fall," a broker said.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7115 marks and 122.12 yen, compared with 1.6941 and 120.92 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 28.1 points at 4,335.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 27.85 points at 2,628.11.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 45.22 points at 3,309.58.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened at $362.40 compared with London's previous close of $362.25. Silver was at $5.31 . REUTER
